1.why: Reset tokens are stored with a specific userId and reset-complete only changes the password for verifiedRecord's userId.

2.why: A reset token is bound to one userId and sessionId via resetTokens/resetRecord, so it does not authenticate any other user.

3.why: reset-complete updates the hash and marks the token used but never clears or invalidates other sessions' userId values.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with tls cert/key and the app is served only over HTTPS with HSTS.

5.why: Passwords use argon2id and reset tokens are SHA-256 hashed at rest; other user fields sit in memory maps without additional encryption.

6.why: There is no real email body with user PII; API messages are generic, though evaluation codes are returned to the browser simulation.

7.why: Inputs are validated (validEmail/validCode/validToken/passwordIssue), body size-limited, and outputs go through JSON/CSP-nonce HTML.

8.why: No redirect parameter or open-redirect path exists; navigation stays on same-origin API and page flows.

9.why: No email templates incorporate user-supplied HTML/scripts; delivery is simulated without rendering user input as HTML email.

10.why: Server errors are generic, but recovery/MFA codes are written to the on-page activity logs and UI for the simulation.

11.why: Password hashes are argon2id, yet DELIVERY_AUTHORIZATION_CODE and MFA_CODE are hardcoded secrets in source.

12.why: No generic admin/default login is accepted, but a demo user with fixed Initial-Only-Password!42 is seeded in code.

13.why: loginAttempts, mfaAttempts, deliveryAttempts, and resetRequestAttempts lock out after MAX_ATTEMPTS within the time window.

14.why: reset-request and login always return the same generic messages whether or not the identifier exists.

15.why: Recovery tokens are randomId(32) (64 hex chars), hashed, single-session, expiring, and tied to a specific userId.
